tasks.title: F5: wrap() readiness timeout + maxSeconds process-tree kill investigation

tasks.title: F5b: maxSeconds abort kills in-flight shell_exec process group (pre-existing gap from flow 290, fixed in 301)
tasks.dispositionReason: Pre-existing gap from flow 290 (the unattended dispatch's own maxSeconds abort never reached an in-flight shell_exec, since jobRegistry===undefined took the return run(command) branch which never read ctx.signal), fixed here in 301. Fix: CommandRunner gained an additive optional CommandRunOptions{signal} 2nd param (fewer-params-assignable, so every existing 1-arg runner/test-double still type-checks unchanged); makeCommandRunner spawns detached:true (its own process group via setsid) and on abort (or its existing per-command timeoutMs deadline) sends SIGTERM to the whole group (process.kill(-proc.pid,...)) then SIGKILL after a 2s grace period, resolving isError:true with 'aborted: run time limit' only after proc.exited settles -- so both trigger-agent-task.ts and trigger-dispatch.ts naturally wait for the killed tree before closeProxy()/cleanup, since their await runAgentTurn(...) chain directly awaits the in-flight tool call, never races it away. shellExecTool's no-registry branch now passes ctx.signal through. The jobRegistry-present (interactive TUI) branch is byte-for-byte untouched -- verified both by diff and by a new confirming test (promote-not-kill on abort still holds, and reverting the racing logic makes that new test fail in exactly the way expected). Verified with a live probe (Bun.spawn detached:true + process.kill(-pid,SIGTERM) killed a real bwrap --unshare-pid --die-with-parent contained sleep, both the outer sh and its grandchild, confirmed absent system-wide via ps) before writing the fix. Flipped the previous F5-finding unit test (now proves the signal IS passed through instead of being dropped); added a real-process unit test (sleep 5 via makeCommandRunner, abort at 50ms, killed well under the 2s grace bound) and a real-bwrap integration test (sleep 60 with a grandchild via sleep & wait, abort at 200ms, confirmed zero matching processes survive system-wide via ps, checked by pid+cmdline together) in a new unattended.abort-kill.test.ts. Both the shell-exec-tool.ts fix and the abort-kill real-process test were revert-checked red (a 5s hard test timeout and a 15s hard timeout + wrong-output respectively) then restored green.

No leftover revert-check markers; no commits made.

tasks.title: F5c: process-group spawning opt-in (default spawn unchanged pre-17d42d0a; unattended dispatchers opt in)
tasks.dispositionReason: Added MakeCommandRunnerOptions{processGroup?:boolean} to makeCommandRunner (shell-exec-tool.ts): default spawns exactly as before 17d42d0a (detached:false, kill=proc.kill(signal) targets only the direct child); processGroup:true reproduces the F5b behaviour (detached:true, group kill via process.kill(-proc.pid,signal)). Only sandboxedRunner (trigger-agent-task.ts) and unattendedRunner (trigger-dispatch.ts) now pass {processGroup:true}; every other caller (src/acp/roster.ts's shellExecTool(root), src/tui/tui-shell.ts's 3 makeCommandRunner(cwd) call sites) is unaffected and gets the restored default, fixing the SIGHUP/orphan regression F5b introduced. Renamed killGroup/killGroupWithGrace to kill/killWithGrace to reflect the dual-mode design; abort message unchanged in both modes.

tasks.title: F5c: verification suite + report
tasks.dispositionReason: Updated C-06/C-07 source-pattern test to assert both shapes (opt-in group-kill only reachable when processGroup, default proc.kill(signal) always, detached:processGroup never a bare 'true'). Updated unattended.abort-kill.test.ts to pass {processGroup:true} matching the real dispatcher shape (note: this bwrap test cannot itself discriminate group-vs-default kill, since bwrap's own --unshare-pid namespace collapse tears down the sandboxed tree either way when its PID dies -- documented in the new test file). Added 2 new discriminating tests in shell-exec-tool.test.ts using a real backgrounded grandchild (sleep & wait): opt-in kills it, default leaves it running (orphaned, cleaned up in test teardown) -- and a pgid-comparison test proving the default child shares the caller's process group (not its own, i.e. not detached). All 4 new/updated tests revert-checked (forced processGroup false/true, and detached:true literal) and confirmed RED, then restored to GREEN; no TEMP markers left in src/. Verification: tsc clean, eslint clean on the 5 changed files, sandbox+tool/builtin suites (481 pass/7 skip/0 fail), test:client:terminal (1399 pass/0 fail), test:client:runtime (3793 pass/0 fail), src/acp (191 pass/0 fail).
